maya: quick heads-up — I ran a set of microbenchmarks comparing FlashAttention v2 vs v3 on the p4d-preempt cluster for the long-chat workload (seq=4096, kv hit ~0.6). numbers look off for v3 when KV cache is hot, can someone sanity-check?
kevin: which metrics are weird? p50/p99 or token throughput?
sanjay: also which kernel build? debug symbols or optimized? memory alloc pattern matters for KV.
maya: baseline runs: v2=3.6ms/token, v3=3.1ms/token for cold KV. but with sustained KV hits we see v3 jump to ~4.4ms/token and increased GPU memcpy stalls. p50 goes up ~40% on long sequences.
julie: can you paste the profile snippet and the exact command you ran?
maya: pasted below — used the nightly flashv3 build with cuda 12.1 kernels. command:
```
./runtest --model=redwood-7b --kernel=flashv3 --seq_len=4096 --batch=4 --kv_hit_rate=0.6 --warm_iters=200 --measure=latency
```
julie: thx. quick profiler output (nvprof-like sampling):
```
Kernel: flash_glam_v3_fused  runtime: 820us  (ideal 480us)
Memcpy H2D stall: 210us
KV lookup: 90us
Allreduce-like sync: 60us
SM occupancy: 78% (should be ~92% for this kernel)
```
kevin: interesting — v3 fused kernel has more memcpy overhead here. could be a path where we write back partial KV pages more often. did you enable paged-attn fallback?
maya: paged-attn disabled for this run. I also tried v3 with paged enabled and latency dropped to ~3.4ms/token (still worse than v2 for sustained kv).
sanjay: hypothesis: flashv3's internal staging buffer + page compaction interacts badly with our KV cache eviction heuristic. when the KV hit ratio is moderate, we end up moving cache pages in/out frequently which triggers extra device-to-host copies.
dmitri: +1. we saw similar pattern in an internal test where fragmentation caused frequent cudaFree/cudaMalloc churn. two mitigation paths: 1) force pinned allocation pool for KV pages, 2) tweak batching window so bigger batches amortize memcpy.
julie: propose short experiment matrix:
- pinned pool vs default alloc
- adaptive_batch_window=50ms vs 20ms
- paged-attn on/off
- flashv2 vs flashv3
We should capture p50/p90/p99 and device memcpy time.
kevin: agree. also add an allocation-trace to see if kernel is triggering small allocations (we have a flag REDWOOD_ALLOC_TRACE).
ops-bot: deploy: started flashv3-nightly to staging (ami: rwinf-flashv3-2026-03-17). CI: 14/16 tests passed — 2 flaky image tests.
maya: good. julie, I've kicked off the matrix runs on p4d-2. I attached the run IDs in the infra dashboard (run: rw-bench-3168-*).
sanjay: FYI memory observation: v3 fused kernel uses ~12% more scratch memory per head which could push some buffers to host if per-GPU reservation < threshold. that matches the memcpy spikes.
dmitri: rollout plan idea (lightweight):
- feature switch name: flash_kernel_variant_v3 (fflag)
- stage 0: internal-only perf tests (done)
- stage 1: canary on non-prod routing (1% traffic), monitor p50, p99, token/sec, kv_evictions/min
- stage 2: ramp 10% with adaptive batching enabled
- rollback triggers: p50 increase >10% OR p99 >20% OR kv_evictions/min >2x baseline OR increase in retransmits/errors >0.3%
julie: add telemetry hooks: per-request kernel id, memcpy_us, kv_copy_us, batch_window_ms. need those logged at 1/10 sampling for perf.
kevin: for canary, we should also pin a few model versions to v2 and v3 and run A/B with same prompts to check generation quality differences (just in case fused kernel subtly changes numerics).
maya: action items:
- julie: add telemetry (kernel id + memcpy/kvcopy counters) — ETA 1 day
- kevin: add REDWOOD_ALLOC_TRACE runs & post allocation traces — ETA today
- sanjay: try pinned allocation pool experiment + reprun matrix — ETA tomorrow
- dmitri: draft rollout playbook with fflag gating and rollback thresholds — ETA EOD
kevin: I'll watch the staging canary once ops-bot finishes deploy.
maya: cheers. if anyone sees degradation in staging, ping me @maya immediately and flip the flag off. :thumbsup:
julie: noted, I'll add a smoke test that runs a 10k token chat replay against both kernels during canary to detect throughput/latency regressions early.
sanjay: one more note — if pinned pool fixes memcpy, we should upstream an allocator change in runtime rather than relying on pinned pool toggles.
dmitri: agreed. we'll treat pinned pool as temporary mitigant.
kevin: ok landing this thread — will post raw bench outputs to the perf board when runs complete.
maya: thanks team.
